independent_read_extent: All ten physical pages of official DJV submission, including complete management, conservation and monitoring context.
Original BfN715 study physical7,46–51 and discussion physical58–62, plus annual-survival and scenario tables; not a full88-page read.
checks: The source scenario reduces survival across all age classes; approximately40% is total annual juvenile/subadult mortality, paired with approximately30% adult mortality. It is not an experimentally established additional harvest allowance.

The author immediately describes the study threshold as mortality, which makes the distinction visible to a reader; the proposed harvest wording nevertheless puts the same rounded number beside shooting.

Up to permits a smaller harvest. The author expressly requires cross-revier shooting plans, monitoring of found dead animals, road deaths and harvested animals, exchange with neighbouring populations, and ongoing conservation assessment. These are affirmative benign context, not merely missing evidence.

The study does not directly test the author’s selected age-class harvest, and underdetermination of that scenario cannot establish that the proposal would destabilise a population. Timing, additive versus compensatory mortality and adult survival matter.
The draft itself requires compatibility with favourable conservation status and contains no statutory40% quota. Later amendments were not substituted.
adjudication: Do not promote. The numerical ecological rationale needs clarification, but the full submission can reasonably be read as an adjustable upper bound implemented through monitored plans. Calling it an additional40% allowance would assert an unresolved interpretation. Preserve the total-mortality distinction and potential materiality, without claiming an inevitable population decline or a correct alternative harvest quota.
quotation_policy: No additional original-source quotations reproduced in this review.

followup.additional_primary: Official oral hearing protocol physical11–12, Dammann-Tamke answers on juvenile intervention and monitoring.
followup.assessment: Independently read the protocol passages. The speaker repeatedly frames40% in terms of population increase and links its measurement to monitoring. This is not identical to the written cohort formulation and supplies further reason not to impose an additional40%-of-whole-cohort interpretation on a concrete management plan. It is context rather than an invented author response to this screen.
